Grade 3 · Unit 3.3

Life Cycles and Traits

How do living things grow, and why are offspring like but not exactly like their parents?

Concept 1

Life cycles are diverse but share stages

A frog, a bean plant, and a mealworm beetle have different life cycles, but all include birth, growth, reproduction, and death.

Diagram

Frog life cycle

eggs, tadpole, froglet, adult frog.

“A frog changes as it grows.”

Try it

Build three models

picture cards for frog, bean plant, and mealworm beetle.

“Put the pictures in order. Find the stages.”

Data

Shared stages chart

columns for Begin, Grow, Reproduce, Die.

“A bean seed sprouts. It grows. It makes new seeds. A mealworm becomes a beetle. All life cycles have stages.”

Concept 2

Offspring inherit traits but vary

Young organisms often get traits from parents, but they are not exact copies.

Try it

Trait survey

beans of different colors/sizes.

“Sort beans. They are similar but not identical.”

Data

Parent-offspring table

parent bean plants and the colors of their offspring seeds.

“Most baby seeds match the parent. Some are different.”

Data

Trait chart

chart of seed colors or leaf shapes.

“Variation is normal.”

Concept 3

Environment can influence traits

The same kind of plant can grow differently in sun and in shade; environment can change how a trait shows up.

Try it

Sun vs shade beans

two cups with beans, one in light, one in dark or shade.

“Same seeds. Same water. One in sun. One in shade.”

You did this before / what is new: You grew beans in 2-B to ask what plants need; now you use the evidence to explain environment-influenced traits.

Data

Provided plant-height data

table with sun plants and shade plants.

“The shade plant stretched taller, but its stem was thin and its leaves were small. The sun plant was shorter and sturdier. The environment changed how the plant grew.”

Real world

Michigan garden

garden plants in a sunny yard and a shady yard.

“Same kind of plant. Different light. Different growth.”

Hands-on · Design or investigate

Try it at home or in class

Fair test: Does light affect bean sprout growth? Change only light. Keep water, container, and seed type the same. Measure and graph sprout height, record color and stem thickness, or use the provided dataset if time or weather is a problem.

Try it

What you need

bean seeds, clear cups, paper towels or soil, water, magnifier, index cards, tape, pictures or drawings of frog, bean plant, and mealworm beetle life stages.

Safety: do not eat seeds; wash hands after handling soil.

Try it

What you do

build life-cycle models; sort beans or leaves by traits; analyze parent-offspring data; grow or examine beans in sun and shade.

No time or no good weather? Use this data

This data is a backup. It lets you practice reading evidence, but the standard expects you to collect your own when you can.

students record seed traits and plant height if growing beans.

parent-offspring bean data: yellow parent produces 8 yellow and 2 green offspring seeds; green parent produces 9 green and 1 yellow; spotted parent produces 6 spotted and 4 yellow. Sun/shade data: same seed type, same water, sun plant 18 cm with a thick green stem and wide leaves; shade plant 22 cm with a thin pale stem and small leaves, after two weeks.

Near you: Michigan dry bean fields: bean seeds from parent plants can show different seed-coat colors and sizes, giving students real trait data.

Words to know

life cycle
stages of growth and reproduction.
trait
a feature like color or shape.
inherit
receive traits from parents.
offspring
young organism.
variation
differences among individuals.
environment
the place and conditions around an organism.
evidence
data that help support a claim.
model
a representation that helps explain an idea.
reproduce
make new organisms or seeds.
growth
getting bigger or changing.
Tutor notes: misconceptions, standards, pacing

Pacing: five 30-minute sessions.

Common misconceptions to listen for:

  • “All life cycles look the same.” Correct: life cycles are diverse, but all include birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
  • “Offspring are exact copies of parents.” Correct: offspring inherit traits but also vary.
  • “Environment cannot change traits.” Correct: environment can influence how some traits show up.
  • “Plants eat soil.” Correct: plants use water, air, and light to grow; soil provides support and minerals.

Limits and cautions:

  • This unit does not teach cells; full cell work belongs in later grades.
  • It does not teach genetics mechanisms or natural selection. Those come later.
  • Plant growth can take days; the provided dataset guarantees evidence if plants grow slowly.
  • The idea that environment influences traits is simplified to visible growth differences.

Michigan Science Standards this unit earns:

  • 3-LS1-1: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles but all share birth, growth, reproduction, and death.
  • 3-LS3-1: Analyze data to provide evidence that organisms inherit traits from their parents.
  • 3-LS3-2: Use evidence to support the explanation that traits can be influenced by the environment.
  • 3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out a fair test when students investigate sun vs shade plant growth.

Connections: Builds on: K-C Living Things and Their Homes; 1-B Parts, Parents, and Young; 2-B Plants, Animals, and Habitats. Builds toward: 3.4 Survival, Fossils, and Change; 5.3 Energy and Matter in Ecosystems; Unit 7 Cells; Unit 8 Classifying Life.

After the lesson · Activity

Play: Trait Family

Some traits come from parents. Others change because of where and how a living thing lives. Which is which?
